# iq_formats_sigmf_oracle — provenance

Used by `tests/iq_formats.rs` (multi-channel SigMF and the `cu8` data type read by
`kshana::iq::io`).

* `third_party/mc3_ci16.sigmf-{meta,data}` and `third_party/cu8.sigmf-{meta,data}` were
  written by **sigmf-python 1.13.0** (LGPL-3.0), run as a tool by
  `gen_iq_formats_sigmf_oracle.py`; no sigmf-python code is linked into or copied into
  the crate. The sample values are synthetic (a counting pattern), generated by the script.
* `reference.json` holds what sigmf-python reads back from those files
  (`fromfile(..., autoscale=False).read_samples()`): per channel, the SHA-256 of the
  little-endian f64 I, Q stream, the sample count, captures and annotations.

sigmf-python returns a multi-channel recording as an array of shape (instants, channels),
which is the indexing `kshana::iq::io::sigmf_stream` uses (a sample index counts time
instants). With `autoscale=False` sigmf-python returns the raw unsigned code `c` for `cu8`;
kshana decodes the same byte to the odd level `2c − 255` (see `iq::io::format`), so the test
compares `2·c − 255`.

Regenerate: `python3 gen_iq_formats_sigmf_oracle.py` with sigmf==1.13.0 and numpy.
